newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Boston Consulting backs Hungary's potential.
newsitem.headline: Boston Consulting backs Hungary's potential.

text.p: Boston Consulting Group said on Monday it saw Hungary as an increasingly competitive player in the global economy and announced the formal opening of its Budapest office.

"There are international companies, our clients in other parts of the world, who are seriously interested in investing here, in understanding the market and using it as part of their system," John Clarkeson, chief executive officer of Boston Consulting, said at a news conference.
"Secondly, we expect that Hungarian enterprises will increasingly be effective eventually on a scale larger than Hungary by itself, both regionally...and globally," Clarkeson said.

John Lindquist, senior vice president, said the company had spent several years building up personnel trained in offices elsewhere, including London, Chicago and Germany, and that there would be a staff of 10 in Budapest by year's end.
"People have already placed bets that Hungary is going to be a very attractive place to do manufacturing," Clarkeson added.
"I think there is a consensus that the growth rates will be no longer negative, they will be positive. Inflation continues to come down.

"It will be easier to finance small and medium sized enterprise and that's a formula that works. And the Hungarians have shown the political will to deal with a lot of the difficult restructuring questions, the budget questions. You'd have to say the flags are flying the right direction."
Boston Consulting has been active in central and eastern Europe since 1985, advising on acquisitions and restructuring, including projects in the banking field, company officials said.

The firm is focusing work for large Hungarian and international companies with priorities in energy, telecommunications, automobiles, financial services, phramaecuticals and consumer goods, a company statement said.
Consulting assignments include advising and implementing recommendations in strategy, reorganisation, re-engineering, acquisition and integration, the statement said.
